Convert a Z3 value to an R value

Source: R/expressions.R
z3_value.Rd

Converts a value expression, typically the result of z3_eval(), to the closest R type that represents it exactly.

Usage

z3_value(x, exact = TRUE, signed = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A z3_expr that is a value.

exact

If FALSE, numbers that are not exactly representable as doubles (including algebraic numbers) are rounded to a nearby double.

signed

For bit-vectors, interpret the bits as a two's complement signed number.

Value

An R value; see the table.

Details

Z3 valueR result
BoolTRUE or FALSE
Int, Real, bit-vectora double when exactly representable; otherwise a gmp::bigz or gmp::bigq if gmp is installed, or else a character string holding the exact value ("1/3")
algebraic numbererror when exact = TRUE; a nearby double when exact = FALSE
String, charactera UTF-8 character string (an error for a string containing U+0000, which R cannot hold)
finite field elementits representative in [0, p), as for Int
Complexan R complex number when both parts are exactly representable doubles (rounded when exact = FALSE)
floating pointa double (NaN, Inf, -0 included); formats wider than double precision only when the value fits exactly, or rounded when exact = FALSE
rounding modeits name, such as "roundNearestTiesToEven"

A double is "exactly representable" when its numerator has absolute value at most 2^53 and its denominator is a power of two up to 2^1023 (subnormal values, with larger denominators, give a bigq); for example 1/4 converts to 0.25, but 1/3 does not convert to 0.3333... unless exact = FALSE.

Symbolic expressions are not values: evaluate them in a model first.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
z3_value(z3_int_val(ctx, 42))
#> [1] 42
z3_value(z3_real_val(ctx, "1/4"))
#> [1] 0.25
z3_value(z3_real_val(ctx, "1/3"), exact = FALSE)
#> [1] 0.3333333
z3_value(z3_bv_val(ctx, 255, 8), signed = TRUE)
#> [1] -1
